reason: I would install the portable zip and test it on a real shoot because 40-50 ms next/back is exactly what I care about, but nothing in the list tells me it can replace what I use XnView MP for: metadata and batch work on my culling folders. Until I have seen it handle a few thousand RAWs, it stays a side tool.
why_switch_or_not: What pulls me in is the speed and that RAW and JPG always show as separate pictures, which is how I cull. What stops me from making it default is that there is no mention of ratings, labels or metadata editing, only an editor, ICC and batch rename/convert, and the benchmark is the developer's own numbers on one PC. I would probably use it for quick double-click opens from Explorer and keep XnView MP for the metadata and batch jobs.
current_app_pros: XnView MP reads nearly everything, has a solid thumbnail browser, batch convert, and metadata/IPTC tools that I rely on every week. It is stable on big folders and I know its shortcuts by heart.
current_app_pains: It is not snappy. Startup and the first RAW preview in a big folder lag, and holding next on full-size RAWs stutters, which I notice. The UI is also cluttered with panels I never use.
objection: One developer, version 0.4.1, and no sign that it covers the metadata and culling side. I do not want to depend on it for a paid shoot and find a gap halfway through a job.
would_change_my_mind: Proof on my own RAW folders (thousands of files, next/back stays under 100 ms with full RAW preview) plus metadata and rating support that matches XnView MP, so I could drop it.
